problem: Simulation policies fail physically because perception, embodiment, dynamics and controller gaps coexist; naive fine-tuning on sparse human corrections can damage a useful base policy.
contribution: TRANSIC trains a deployable student through action-space distillation and learns a gated residual policy from online human corrections.
algorithm: Train a privileged RLteacher with operational-space control, record its joint behavior and distill a point-cloud student into joint-position control. Fit a residual to pre/post-intervention state differences and a gate deciding when to apply that correction while preserving thebase.
observations: Teacher privileged simulator state; student synthetic/real point clouds and proprioception, with matched point-cloud feature regularization. A visualRGBstudent is a different adaptation, not exactTRANSIC replication.
actions: Teacher operational-space actions are relabelled to joint-position targets; residuals represent human correction differences, with discrete gripper semantics treated separately.
embodiment_and_data: FurnitureBench manipulation: stabilize, reach/grasp, insert andscrew. Respectively20/100/90/17real correction trajectories yield62/434/489/58correction events.
experiments: Real-robot evaluation uses20trials per condition with varied initial object/robot poses; compare sim-to-real gaps, correction budget, gating and base-policy preservation, and demonstrate longer composed assemblies.
baselines: Direct transfer, domain randomization/data augmentation,BC/IQL fine-tuning,HG-DAgger/IWR andreal-onlyBC/BC-RNN/IQL.

quantitative_result.reason: Comparisons and20trialprotocol examined; exact per-taskbar values were notdigitized.

limitations: Human synchronization and point-cloud calibration are prerequisites; unsafe naive deployment is explicitly rejected. Simulation controller fidelity, limitedcorrections and asset coverage constraintransfer. Broad real-world robustness is not a guarantee for another robot.
hardware_adaptation: Adapt teacher/student action parity and correction provenance. Do not install the full simulationstack or assume theNano/SO101 supports its controller. AnRGB-onlycompactACTbaseline must be explicitly recorded as a different implementation choice.
algorithm_detail: Student training combines behavior-cloning likelihood with aligned point-cloud feature regularization. The residual learns generalized pre/post-state differences, while a learned gate controls intervention; keeping baseandresidual separate limits destructive full-policyupdates. Teacher/controlleraction relabeling is fundamental to parity.
integration_contract: Store requested/accepted/dispatched actions, pre/post-correction states, takeover indicators, sourcepolicy, point-cloud/camera registration and actionmapping. Only actually measured states may be called jointfeedback; command estimates remain explicit.
license_evidence: OfficialGitHub metadata identifiesMIT at thepinnedhead. Sourceinstallation, weights/data rights andNX/hardware execution were not audited, so no fullupstreamparity is asserted.
required_experiments: Teacher/student executor parity; no privilegedobservation leakage; correctionrouting; full-finetune versus gatedresidual retention; identifiedsimfaultablation; independent outcomes under matchedtargetdata andresources.
difference_from_explorer: Simteachers, visualstudents and gatedhumanrepair are published priorwork. Explorer needs a separately tested evidence-memory, cross-embodiment or diagnosis result.
